title: Free first, late plans after
igCaption:
Free Greek festival, then late-night plans.
Nov. 6 to 9, South Florida, $0 to $60

Sources: Miami New Times

#SouthFlorida #MiamiEvents #WeekendGuide #ThingsToDo

scenes.text: Free Greek festival first, then the after-dark picks after dinner.

location.name: Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation

scenes.text: Start Friday at the North Miami Greek Festival. It takes over the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation at 12250 NW Second Ave. Admission is free with RSVP, and the church grounds turn into a Greek village with live music, traditional dancing, homemade meals, raffles, vendors, and guided church tours.

scenes.text: For film, Subtropic Film Festival opens its fourth installment Friday with Homegrown. That block has five short films from five directors. This year’s theme is Between Two Waters, focused on where the ocean and the Everglades meet. Tickets run $10 to $30 at various venues.

scenes.text: Saturday night, Pinecrest Gardens starts its 17th annual Jazz at Pinecrest Gardens season at 8 p.m. Singer Allyson Briggs and Big Band leader Dan Gabel open with America: Together in Harmony, built around the Great American Songbook. Tickets cost $45 to $60. If you’re there Saturday, check NEAR after the set to spot familiar faces.

scenes.text: Sunday at 7 p.m., Fall for Dance Now! hits the Miami Beach Bandshell at 7275 Collins Ave. Dance Now! Miami gives a preview of its 27th season with excerpts from Clara and work from the company’s Youth Ensemble. Tickets cost $10 to $25.
